LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Grid.Events.Desc: A click goes to the deepest element under the cursor: a nested button takes it from the block it sits in. Among overlapping siblings the priority comes from zOrder, which drives both draw order and who receives the click and the cursor.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Grid.AutoHeight.Desc: autoHeight makes height follow content, both for table rows and for containers: RowHeight becomes a minimum rather than the size. An explicit height disables the flag; maxHeight caps the growth.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Grid.Wrap.Desc: wrapChildren moves children that do not fit the container width onto the next line. Without it they are squeezed to fit. With wrapping, grow stretches items within their own line.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Classes.Desc: A class is a named set of properties an element can take on and swap at runtime. Which one wins: code defaults, then the theme, then classes in list order, and above all the style set on the element itself. Declare a class in code (Theme.DefineClass) or in a theme file, where its name starts with '#'.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Limits.Desc: minWidth / maxWidth / minHeight / maxHeight clamp the resulting size. They apply both with an explicit width/height and without one; on conflict the minimum wins.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Nav.Forms.Label: Label (field label)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Shell.Title: RimUI Framework — component showcase
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Theme.TemplateCopied: [RimUI] Copied theme template ({0} chars) to the clipboard
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Grid.Columns.Title: 12-column grid
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Grid.Columns.Desc: Give each element a span from 1 to 12 columns. When a row runs out of room, the remaining elements wrap automatically.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Grid.Span.Title: 3 × 2 rows
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Grid.Span.Desc: Grid cells can span columns horizontally and rows vertically. The remaining cells flow around the merged area automatically.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Grid.Nested.Desc: A grid cell can contain another grid (left) or a stretching flex layout with space-between distribution (right).
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Radius.Title: Corner radius
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Radius.Desc: Corner radius comes from the theme: none, small, middle, or large. The theme defines the actual pixel values.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Gradients.Desc: An element can use a vertical, horizontal, or diagonal linear gradient. The border gradient is configured separately from the background.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Shadows.Desc: Shadows support custom blur, offset, and opacity. This example uses a light backdrop so the shadow is easy to see.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Opacity.Desc: Backgrounds can be translucent. These three examples use alpha values of 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 over a busy backdrop.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Opacity.Label: background alpha
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.SpriteFrame.Title: Sprite frame (9-slice with overflow)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.SpriteFrame.Desc: This frame comes from a 9-sliced sprite sheet with room for decoration. Blue marks the functional content area; gold marks decorative overflow outside it.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Typography.Desc: Text size, weight, OS font, exact pixel size, and shadow are all controlled through the text element's style.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Label.Desc: A field label can include a leading icon, a required-field asterisk, and a hint below the main label.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Checkbox.Desc: A checkbox toggles a yes/no value. State can live in the element or come from your code; disabled state and theme sprites are supported.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Radio.Desc: Radio buttons share one group value, so selecting one clears the others in that group. The ring and inner dot can use theme sprites.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Switch.Desc: A pill-shaped switch toggles on and off; its thumb glides to the active side. Disabled state and theme sprites are supported.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ToggleButton.Desc: A toggle button has two captions, such as On and Off. Clicking it flips the state and swaps the caption.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Slider.Desc: Drag the thumb to change the value. Sliders support steps, units, tick marks, end labels, two-thumb ranges, and disabled state.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.InputText.Desc: A single-line input can have a placeholder, a bound value, an icon, read-only or disabled state, and a custom frame sprite.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.InputNumber.Desc: A numeric field with +/− buttons. It supports integers, decimals, custom steps, and min/max limits.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Textarea.Desc: A fixed-height multiline input for longer text. Height is set as a number of visible rows.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Select.Desc: Click the field to open a list, then click an option to select it and close the panel. Supports placeholders, long searchable lists with scrolling, custom frame sprites, and disabled state.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.MultiSelect.Desc: Pick several values from one list. Selected items appear as removable chips inside the field; overflow collapses into “+N”. The panel stays open after each pick and supports search and a selection limit.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.MultiTreeSelect.Desc: Select multiple leaves from a tree. Clicking a leaf toggles it, selected leaves appear as chips in the field, and search matches leaf names.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.SelectButton.Desc: A joined row of button segments for choosing exactly one value. Selecting a segment deactivates the rest.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.TreeSelect.Desc: A select field whose dropdown contains a tree instead of a flat list. Expand branches and click any node to select it.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.CascadeSelect.Desc: Cascading selection through nested submenus. Hovering a parent opens the next level beside it; clicking a leaf completes the selection.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ColorPicker.Desc: Color picker with an HSB square, a hue strip, an alpha slider, and manual hex input. There is no eyedropper for sampling the screen.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Tag.Desc: A non-interactive status label. Severity controls its color, and an icon can be added. Tags do not handle clicks.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chip.Desc: An interactive pill on a neutral background. It can include an icon and a working remove button, useful for clearing selected tags.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Badge.Desc: A circular counter over another element. It can show a number or a plain dot, for example to mark unread items.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.InlineMessage.Desc: An in-flow notification, not a popup. Severity controls its color and icon; it can be dismissible and use a theme sprite.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Meter.Desc: A bar split into proportional segments, such as the makeup of a stockpile, with a legend below. Each segment color comes from your data.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ProgressBar.Desc: A progress bar can show a value from 0 to 1 or run in indeterminate mode when the final progress is unknown. Theme sprites are supported.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Spinner.Desc: A spinning loading ring with configurable size, speed, and color.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Panel.Desc: A panel with a header and any body content. Collapsible panels hide or reveal their body when the header is clicked.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Panel.BodyIsAnyElement: The body can be any element.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Accordion.Section2: Section 2. Opening it closes the others.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Accordion.Desc: Each section has a header and body. Clicking the header opens it; with Multiple=false, opening one section closes the others.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Tabs.Desc: Click a tab header to switch content. Tabs can sit on the top, bottom, left, or right; the active tab visually joins the body.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ListBox.Desc: Click a row to select it, Ctrl-click to toggle it, Shift-click to select a range, and assign your own action to double-click.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.OrderList.Desc: A reorderable list. Move rows with the up/down buttons or drag them with the mouse.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.PickList.Desc: Move items between two lists using the center buttons or by double-clicking. Ctrl and Shift let you move several items at once.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Tree.Desc: A tree with expandable branches. The left example supports multi-selection and leaf search; the right uses checkboxes that include all descendants.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.DataTable.Desc: A table with zebra rows, hover highlighting, multi-selection, sorting by the Lvl header, AND-combined Colonist and Skill filters, and live UI elements inside cells instead of plain text.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.TreeTable.Desc: A table whose first column is an expandable tree and whose other columns are regular data cells. Sorting by Category or Amount only reorders siblings under the same parent; the Category filter searches tree leaves.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Button.Desc: Buttons support ready-made color presets, icons on either side of the caption, disabled state, and tooltips. They size to their content instead of stretching horizontally.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Popover.BodyText: A line of text in the popup.\nClamped to the window bounds.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Popover.Desc: A popup panel anchored to a point, usually a button. It opens on click, can contain anything, and closes when you click outside it.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.DropdownMenu.Desc: A button-triggered dropdown whose items can be disabled or open nested submenus on hover.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Menu.Desc: Menus can be static and embedded in the UI flow (left), or contextual and opened with the right mouse button (right).
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Tooltip.ClickPassesThroug: The click reaches the button; the tooltip does not capture input.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Tooltip.Desc: A tooltip template can contain anything, follows the cursor, and does not capture clicks, so you can click the element underneath it.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Icons.Desc: Fetch an icon from the built-in sheet with Icons.Get(index), then set its size, tint, and rotation. The same icons can be placed inside buttons.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ModalWindow.Desc: A modal has a header with a menu button, centered title, and close button; a body that scrolls when needed; and an action footer. Drag it by the header.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.MessageWindow.Desc: A message window is a simpler modal with no hamburger menu and a single close action in the footer. It can have its own style and frame sprite.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.MessageWindow.InfoDesc: An informational window with one footer button that closes it.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ConfirmWindow.Desc: A confirmation window has separate accept and reject actions. It can have its own style and frame sprite.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ConfirmWindow.ConsentDesc: Accept and reject are separate events. Close and Esc both count as reject.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ModalWindow.Example.Desc: A complete modal with a header, a scrollable body, and a footer. It can only be dragged by the header; Esc closes it.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ModalWindow.Example.Title: Modal title
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ProgressBar.VerticalNote: vertical: fills from bottom to top
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Slider.VerticalNote: vertical: single and range (min at bottom)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.SpriteTiling.Desc: Sprite edges and centers can repeat as tiles instead of stretching. Partial tiles are clipped, not squashed. This example repeats teeth and dots in 3-unit modules.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.Title: Component events
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.Desc: Every component has an Events block for hover enter/leave/per-frame, left and right clicks, scrolling, disabled-state changes, and selection. The callback receives the component and event data. Events are observers: built-in behavior runs first, then your callback.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.ButtonBlock: button: hover enter/leave/per-frame and LMB/RMB clicks
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.DisabledBlock: disabled state: the switch disables the checkbox, which fires an event
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.ListBlock: list: selection (index + value) and scroll, including internal scrolling
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.LogEmpty: No events yet. Hover, click, and select items above.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Methods.Title: Component methods
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Methods.Desc: Read and write values directly from code with GetValue()/SetValue() on fields and toggles, or GetSelected()/SetSelected() on selection components. SetStyle("path", "value") changes styles using the same paths and formats as a theme file; put the component part first, for example box.borderColor. Invalid paths are silently ignored.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Methods.ResultEmpty: result: — (click one of the Read buttons)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.CircularProgress.Desc: A circular progress bar with configurable arc shape, start point, direction, along-arc gradient, track borders, and centered text or icon.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Animations.Desc: Wrap any element in Animated and attach a built-in module by name. Custom modules are registered through Animations.Register in exactly the same way.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Animations.EntranceNote: entrance: fade-in | slide-in-left | fade-in-up | pop icon (restart with button)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.SegmentProgress.Desc: A segmented progress bar fills whole segments rather than a continuous strip. Each segment can have its own color; horizontal, vertical, and circular layouts are available.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Image.Desc: Display an image by texture key with regular spacing, radius, and border styles. Fit modes include stretch, contain, and cover with cropping.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.CustomDraw.Desc: Custom drawing: OnDraw uses framework commands that work across themes and UI scales; OnDrawNative gives direct access to RimWorld GUI/Widgets when you need full control.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Gallery.Desc: An image gallery with a large central frame, side arrows, and a thumbnail strip for quick navigation. It can also advance automatically on a timer.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AudioPlayer.Desc: An audio helper for playlists stored in your mod's Audio/ folder (ogg/wav/mp3), with Play/Pause/Next/Prev/Seek methods. It is not a ready-made player UI; build that from RimUI components.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AudioPlayer.NoFilesHint: Put .ogg, .wav, or .mp3 files in the mod's Audio/ folder to try the player here.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.NodeCanvas.Desc: A draggable node-and-link canvas. Z-index controls overlap order; smooth links run from a node's output on the right to another node's input on the left, with per-type limits. The entire canvas can be saved to and loaded from JSON.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.NodeCanvas.ControlsHint: drag — move; » — choose a link type, then click a highlighted target (RMB cancels); RMB a link — delete; RMB empty space — add node; X — delete node
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.NodeCanvas.DeleteBlockDes: The node and all of its links will be deleted.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.NodeCanvas.CopiedMessage: [RimUI] Copied canvas state to the clipboard
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.NodeCanvas.Config.Title: Node settings
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chart.Radar.Desc: Charts support multiple data series, including live values updated every frame through a provider, plus legends, automatic value scales, and hover tooltips. Supply data from code or flat JSON.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chart.Radar.Note: Radar: 2 code-defined series; the last value in series 2 is live (hover the vertices)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chart.Polar.Note: PolarArea: data loaded from a JSON string (labels + series); categories in the legend (hover sectors)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Animations.StyleAnimNote: Define an animation as a string in a style or theme (Style.Animation or "animation" in theme JSON), with no extra code
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chart.Pie.Desc: A single series divides the circle into sectors proportional to category values. Donut mode does the same with a cutout in the center.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chart.Line.Desc: Line draws an unfilled outline; Area uses the same curve but fills the space down to the zero line.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chart.Column.Desc: Column draws values as vertical bars rising upward; Bar displays the same data as horizontal bars.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chart.Heatmap.Desc: A colonist × day matrix. Each cell interpolates between MinColor and MaxColor according to its value; values near the maximum approach MaxColor.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Chart.Heatmap.Caption: Recreation hours this week
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Wrap.Off: wrapChildren = false - all seven squeeze into one line
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Wrap.On: wrapChildren = true - the same seven wrap
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Wrap.Grow: wrapChildren together with grow - stretching works within its own line, not across the whole block
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Wrap.SegOff: SelectButton, wrapChildren = false - the segments squeeze
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Wrap.SegOn: SelectButton, wrapChildren = true - they wrap onto the next line
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Wrap.Tabs: Tabs, wrapChildren = true - the tab strip wraps and the body moves down with it
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.SteelDesc: An ordinary material; it fits on one line.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.PlateDesc: A long description that does not fit on one line and wraps onto several: it is exactly what should make the table row grow instead of cutting the text off at a fixed height.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.ListLong: A long caption that does not fit the list's width and wraps
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.TreeDeep: A nested node whose long caption runs out of width
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.Shrink: shrink: a block 150 tall with content taller than that. On the left shrink = 1 - the children squeeze to fit; on the right shrink = 0 - they keep their size and go past the bottom border
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.ScrollBox: ScrollBox in a block 160 tall. On the left autoHeight = false - it fits the block and scrolls; on the right true - it grows to its content and the block clips the excess
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.TableOff: DataTable, autoHeight = false - the row height is fixed and the text is cut off
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.TableOn: DataTable, autoHeight = true - the row grows to its content
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.TreeTable: TreeTable, autoHeight = false on the left, true on the right
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.ListBox: ListBox, autoHeight = false on the left, true on the right - the long caption wraps
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.AutoH.Tree: Tree, autoHeight = false on the left, true on the right. The nested node's caption is wider than the room left after the branch indent
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.OuterHint: a click on the block's background counts for the block
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.BlockClick: A click on the button is counted by the button alone; a click on the background, by the block alone. The cursor differs too: a caret over the block, a hand over the button
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Events.BlockZ: Two overlapping blocks. The green one is declared second and with ZOrder = 5: it is drawn on top and takes the click where they overlap. The red one responds only where the green does not cover it
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.Title: Resizing with the mouse
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.Desc: Style.Resizable lets a block be resized by its frame. The grab zone is the border itself, so the content stays usable: a button at the edge and a scrollbar are clickable as always. Resizing changes only Style.Width/Height, within Min/Max.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.ClickBody: A button inside a resizable block works as usual.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.AllHint: Drag any side or corner. The size is clamped to 90x50 ... 420x220.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.HorzHint: Only the left and right edges can be dragged.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.NoBorderHint: No border is set - there is no grab at all.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.FlowHint: This block's width is handed out by the row (Grow = 1): there is no grab horizontally, but there is vertically.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.WinHint1: Drag the window by any edge or corner. The left and top edges move the position as well: the opposite side stays put.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.WinHint2: The size you drag out is remembered: the window does not jump back to its content-derived size.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.BlockAll: resizable = All - eight directions; corners outrank sides, and the button inside the block keeps working
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.BlockHorz: resizable = Horizontal - the left and right edges only; at the top and bottom the cursor does not change
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.BlockNoBorder: no border is set - there is no resizing: dragging an invisible boundary is not discoverable, nobody would guess where it is
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.BlockFlow: a parent outranks its child - the row hands out the width, so there is no grab horizontally; vertically the block resizes
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Resize.BlockWindow: the window resizes by edges and corners; the dragged size is remembered
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Limits.MaxH: MaxHeight 40, text taller than the box
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Limits.LongText: This text is deliberately taller than the block: it takes six or seven lines while the block has room for two. The upper lines show in both cases, but everything below the block's border behaves differently. With overflow: visible the lines keep being drawn and spill onto whatever sits below - the block does not hold them in. With overflow: clip those same lines are cut off exactly at the block's bottom border, as if they had never been there. The difference between the two blocks is this one flag: the sizes, padding, background and the text itself are identical.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Limits.OvVisible: visible - the lines continue past the block's border
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Limits.OvClip: clip - the same lines are cut off at the border
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Classes.Block: Clicking a card toggles the "selected" class. The third card carries the "disabled" class: it is declared after selected and therefore wins - selecting it does not highlight it
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Flush.Block: flush() and getText() - the button takes what was typed without waiting for Enter or for focus to be lost; the value is read from the field's state, so it is available even when the field is off-screen
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Cascade.BlockClear: clearable - a "nothing selected" first item that clears the selection
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Cascade.BlockBranch: selectBranches - the "Materials" branch can be selected itself and stays expandable
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Cascade.BlockMulti: multiSelect - a click adds to the set, a second one removes; the caption shows how many
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Cascade.BlockApi: SetSelected and Clear from code: the field's caption is taken from the selected item
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Axis.BlockZoom: yMin/yMax/yTickStep and a label format of your own - the axis runs from 20 to 60 in steps of 10, and every label carries its unit
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Axis.BlockRaw: niceTicks = false - the scale ends exactly at the data maximum (19), which makes the step fractional: 4.75, 9.5, 14.25
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Axis.BlockNice: niceTicks (the default) - the step is rounded to 1/2/5*10^n and the top is extended to a whole number of steps: labels 0, 5, 10, 15, 20
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Axis.BlockHeat: yMin/yMax - the colour is computed against a 0..10 scale rather than this map's own data, which makes two maps side by side comparable
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Sort.BlockTable: defaultSortColumn - on first showing, the rows are already ordered by level from highest to lowest; after that the order is set by clicks on the header
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Sort.BlockTree: defaultSortColumn - on first showing, the nodes are already ordered by amount from highest to lowest, within each parent separately
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Header.Launcher: A header of your own: elements around the hamburger, the title and the close button
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Header.OpenButton: Open a window with a custom header
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Header.Body: This window's header adds elements of its own to the built-in ones: a button after the hamburger on the left, a tag beside the title in the centre, and two buttons before "close" on the right. Dragging by the header still works, and pressing the header's buttons does not drag the window.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Header.Title: Custom header
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Header.BeforeTitle: Button to the left of the title
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ScrollBox.Desc: Scrolling for any content: lists, tables, wide diagrams. It works at the core level - children are laid out with a scroll offset and drawing is clipped to the viewport. Horizontal scrolling is switched on by the Horizontal flag (off by default, so that content wraps instead of running off sideways).
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ScrollBox.Both: Both axes: the wheel scrolls vertically, Shift + wheel horizontally
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Cursor.Desc: Style.Cursor sets the MEANING of the cursor (arrow / hand / move / caret / four resize directions), while the theme supplies the texture and the hotspot. Unity gives mods no access to OS cursors, so the framework ships its own assets drawn in the system style - a white body with a black outline. The deepest element under the mouse wins; the shape is applied once per frame.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Cursor.NestArrow: ...while this block brings the arrow back (Arrow)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Cursor.Auto: Unconfigured: the cursor comes from theme slots
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Style.Cursor.NestInner: ...and the field inside claims the caret
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.OrgChart.Desc: A hierarchy diagram: node cards, connecting lines, collapsible subtrees (the circle on the card's edge) and node selection - single, multiple (MultiSelect) and cascading over a whole subtree (SelectChildren). It grows downwards or to the right (Orientation). Selection can be switched off entirely (Selectable on the chart) or per node (Selectable on the node). The chart easily grows wider than the window, so it is wrapped in a ScrollBox with horizontal scrolling - the component itself does not scroll.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.OrgChart.Basic: A basic chart: clicking the circle collapses a branch, clicking the card selects it
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.OrgChart.Horizontal: Horizontal growth plus cascading multi-select: clicking a department marks its subordinates too, clicking again clears them
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.OrgChart.Template: A card template of your own (NodeTemplate)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Rating.Desc: A star rating: the score is set by clicking. The value is fractional, so the component shows halves as well as external scores such as "4.2 out of 5". Clicking the current score again clears it (Cancel), and hovering shows what a click would set.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Rating.Basic: Ordinary: five stars, the value in an external variable
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Rating.Half: Halves (AllowHalf): click the left half of a star
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Paginator.Desc: Page navigation: arrows to the start, back, forward and to the end, page numbers with an ellipsis, and an optional page-size selector. Numbering starts at one - the way the player sees it. The component does not own the data: it reports the chosen number, and your code makes the selection.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Paginator.WithData: With data: the list below is rebuilt from the page number
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Paginator.Many: Many pages: the first and the last are always visible
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Timeline.Desc: An event timeline: markers on an axis, lines between them, content to the side. Vertical and horizontal orientations; content sits on one side or alternates. To the left of the axis is the "opposite side" for a date, a time or a status.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Timeline.Basic: Ordinary: dates on the left, events on the right
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Timeline.Colors: Custom marker colours and the Start side
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.Desc: A step-by-step wizard: a strip of headers with a progress indicator, the active step's content, and moves forward and back. In linear mode jumping ahead over a step is forbidden, and a step can refuse to let you leave until a condition is met (CanLeave). Going back is always allowed - otherwise an unfilled form would become a trap.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.Linear: Linear with validation: steps 2 and 3 do not let you move on until they are filled in
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.FreeLabel: Free mode: click any step, no buttons
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.Step1Body: The first step asks for nothing - just press "Next".
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.NameHint: While the field is empty, "Next" will not work.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.AgreeHint: Without the tick it will not let you move on, but you can still go back.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.Agree: I agree to everything at once
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.Step4Body: The last step: the "Next" button turns into "Finish".
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.Free1Body: The steps are independent, so you can switch between them in any order.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.Free2Body: An icon of your own instead of the number is set by the Icon field.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Stepper.Free3Body: The navigation buttons are off - the headers are the only control.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ConfirmPopup.Desc: A compact confirmation right at the target element: a message and two buttons, with no full-screen modal. It suits reversible local actions; for anything irreversible and important ConfirmWindow remains, which cannot be missed. It closes on a click outside, on a button, or on clicking the target again.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ConfirmPopup.Label: Confirmation at the button: below and to the right
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ConfirmPopup.DeleteMsg: Delete the selected record? This cannot be undone.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ConfirmPopup.ResetMsg: Return the counter to three records?
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.OverlayClip.Block: A Select inside a table cell: the panel opens below the table's body and is clickable all the way down - the ancestors' clipping does not cut it off
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Placement.Down: placement = Bottom - the panel sits under the field, left edges aligned (the default)
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Placement.UpLeft: placement = Top, align = End - the panel sits above the field and runs left: right edges aligned
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Placement.Center: align = Center - the panel is centred on the field even when wider than it
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Placement.Wide: panelWidth = Content - the panel is as wide as its longest item rather than as the narrow field
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Placement.Long2: An improved component with a blueprint
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.PopoverApi.Block: close() from code: picking an item closes the panel, and the button outside opens it and shows what was picked
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Opacity.Desc: Style.Opacity dims an element together with all its children in one value: background, text, image, nested blocks. Style.Tint colours a subtree the same way, with a colour multiplier. Nested values multiply together: 0.5 inside 0.5 gives 0.25, grey inside red gives a muted red. Dropdown panels neither dim nor take the tint - a list over a dimmed card stays readable.
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Opacity.Row: 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.3 - the same card with different dimming
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Opacity.Nested: Nesting: the outer block at 0.5, the inner card at another 0.5 - 0.25 together
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Opacity.Toggle: Dimming by state: the button switches the card between normal and dimmed
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Opacity.Title: Wheat
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Opacity.Tint: Style.Tint - a colour multiplier over the whole subtree: desaturated, shifted to red, shifted to blue
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.Opacity.TintNested: Tint and dimming combine: a red subtree with a dimmed card inside it
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.HScroll.Block: The columns do not fit: the fixed widths plus the minimum share are wider than the table. The content scrolls sideways, and the fade at the edge shows there are more columns to the right
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.HScroll.Name: Name
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ItemContent.SelectBlock: An item with content of its own: a row with a tag and a caption instead of plain text. The selected item is shown the same way in the field itself
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ItemContent.ListBlock: A list row is built by a factory from the value: the row height is measured from the content, while search and sorting still go by the text
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ItemContent.TreeBlock: A node with content of its own: the expand chevron and the branch indent stay in place, the caption is replaced by a composition
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ItemContent.MenuBlock: A menu item with content of its own: the check mark and the submenu arrow stay in place
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ItemContent.HeadBlock: A column header with content of its own: an icon beside the caption. The sort arrow and the filter field stay in place
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ItemContent.TreeTableBloc: A tree-table node with content of its own in the first column: the other columns are given as elements anyway
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ItemContent.PanelBlock: A panel header with content of its own: a caption, a counter and a switch in the header. The collapse chevron stays in place
LanguageData.RimUI.Showcase.ItemContent.ChipBlock: Chip, Tag, InlineMessage and Label accept not just a caption but any composition
